newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday, and the rates are expected to continue to move around the current levels in the next few days due to new A share issues, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 10 percent from 11 percent on Monday.
Turnover fell to 7.19 million lots from 11.61 million lots on Monday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said this week's new A share issues, which suck liquidity out of the repo market, prevented the rates from falling in trading today.
"Early-maturing contracts will move around the 10 percent level in the next few days," one local trader said. "It seems some big non-bank financial institutions have entered the market to buy them."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down with some financial institutions continuing to sell in the market today, traders said.
The most active three-year bond that matures in 1999 closed down to 101.89 yuan from 102.05 yuan on Monday. Turnover of the contract rose to 300 million yuan from 260 million yuan.
The combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.07 million lots from 957,014 lots on Monday.
"Some financial institutions continued to sell on the spot market and the key 10-year contract fell below the 120-yuan level today," one trader said.
